title: C254 — Glove Compartment Lamp
introduction:
I read this little lamp’s connector map as a route through its electrical connections: a battery-saver relay connection and a ground return. The battery saver gives the interior lighting a closing time—the function label identifies its role in switching lighting off, without supplying the timing or control logic.

Start with the connector identity and shell record, then use the face drawing’s cavity labels to find the matching circuit rows. Read across each row to keep its wire identification, function and terminal entry together. The final table identifies the listed service pigtail, a connector assembly with attached repair leads.

This is a connection-reading guide, not a lamp-removal, probing, diagnostic or replacement procedure. Physical viewing direction, operating conditions and test readings are outside its scope. Size and Used codes and the gauge convention remain unexplained reference entries rather than dimensions, test results or wire-selection instructions.

edits.why: The drawing has vertically stacked cavities, a projecting feature on the left and a taller surrounding feature on the right. I use that distinctive outline to recognize the illustration before connecting its cavity labels to the table. Left, right, upper and lower describe the displayed drawing only; they do not establish the installed orientation or which physical side to probe. The harness label and identification row tie the view to its connector record.

The function column separates the battery-saver relay connection from the instrument-panel ground connection. A relay is an electrically controlled switch, but that label does not guarantee a separate plug-in relay. Read each row’s circuit, wire identification and terminal entry together; the terminal entries differ between the connections. The ground wording identifies the recorded return location without showing an access route. These assignments explain the map, not whether the lamp, supply or return has passed a test.

The service-part identifier names the listed repair assembly, and Engineering Shell connects it to the housing record. I keep the pigtail’s gauge and material description separate from the vehicle-wire rows, whose gauge entries differ. The material description belongs to the listed part; it is not an instruction to add grease. This record identifies parts but supplies no wire-selection, terminal-treatment or splicing method.
